Man Utd trigger Fernandes' one-year contract extension
- Published
Manchester United have triggered their one-year option on captain Bruno Fernandes' contract.
The 32-year-old's deal was due to expire next summer but sources say both parties decided it was in their best interests to activate the option through to 2028.
It means overseas clubs will not be able to approach Fernandes when the transfer window opens on 1 January.
The Portugal international confirmed on Tuesday that discussions over a new contract had been paused. Sources say they will resume once United's league position has improved.
Fernandes has made 343 appearances for United, scoring 115 goals, since his £47m move from Sporting in January 2020.
Last season he broke the Premier League assists record and scooped all of the individual player of the year awards after an outstanding campaign as United finished third.
While there is doubt over his long-term future, extending the contract means United would be able to command a fee for Fernandes should he leave in the summer.
United had been open to selling Fernandes in the summer of 2025, with Saudi Pro-League club Al Hilal offering a huge deal.
After discussing the situation with his wife, Fernandes decided to stay, though he later said it "hurt" United were willing to sell him. He reiterated on Tuesday he was still ambitious to win the biggest honours in the game.
Fernandes is a doubt for Saturday's Premier League encounter with Brentford after returning from the Champions League trip to Sporting with a virus.
The playmaker, who scored both goals in the 2-2 draw with his former club, but did not train on Friday and head coach Mauricio Pochettino said he would take a decision on his captain's fitness on Saturday morning.
"We are going to assess during the day and then tomorrow see how he is when he wakes up," said Pochettino. "We are not going to take any risks."
